items.title: Sylvester Handy Interview, 1961-12-13
items.q: I played with Kid Quencher, I played with Kid Rainey, I played with Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: Yes. I tell you what, my mother, I'd go home with 30, 40 dollars and give my mother. And it would seem impossible for us to pick up that kind of money, a piece to go home with. And we have made good money. Made good money. Then I've had cousins and they would likewise. It wasn't three, it was six of us all together. My cousin and I and my brothers. And they'd go around, we called it Surinating and we'd go around Surinating. And we would make, we have made some money during those times. Well, after then, after I…

items.title: Crescent City Crystals: Dave Bailey, Harold Christophe, Albert Delone, Sylvester Handy Interview, 1963-11-13
items.q: I played with, uh, uh, Kid Rainy.

ctx.x: Born in New Orleans and the Trimmy.

Trimmy? Oh, I know. From Trimmy to the Rocky Green. Like London Avenue. 7-Watt, you know? What... Who taught you to play guitar? Now, who taught me how to play guitar? My father played guitar, you see? Yeah. But my first instrument, I used to pick up his guitar. Uh-huh. And all that harmony was right in my head. Yeah. Sure, I guess from listening to him, you pick up... Yeah, and definitely I would get beaten for fooling the guitar. Yeah. You know what I mean? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. But then I started out on the…
